description: E-D at runtime. A binding a scope creates for itself is visible only "from the point the statement that creates it has run", and a block's read of an enclosing binding created later in the enclosing scope is named explicitly as one of the failures that take `ol-undefined-var` rather than the boundary code (spec/execution-model.md:396-403,408-411, spec/error-model.md:102). No procedure is involved, so the boundary cannot be the cause. The existing check fixture `undefined-var-eager-block-reads-a-later-enclosing-binding` makes this claim at the semantic stage over the same program; its description asserts the runtime agrees, and nothing measured that until this fixture. The two stages agree here for the reason spec/execution-model.md:416-424 gives — within one scope's straight-line statement list a conservative lexical checker and an eager evaluator reach the same answer, because no execution order can make the later binding reachable at this read. Added at the logic/spec reviewer's request during the review gate.
